title: HTTP Client
subtitle: Small HTTP requests, directly from DuckDB.
intro: Fetch HTTP resources or submit JSON and form bodies from a SQL expression, through DuckDB's own HTTP stack. Responses arrive as a JSON envelope containing status, reason, headers and body, ready to inspect or save in a local table.

reference.name: http_get(url)
reference.description: Fetch a response; headers and params are optional, by name.

reference.name: http_head(url)
reference.description: Request metadata only; headers return as a JSON object.

reference.name: http_post(url, headers, body)
reference.description: Send a JSON body; headers are MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR).

reference.name: http_put(url, headers, body)
reference.description: Replace a resource; http_delete(url, headers) removes one.

reference.name: http_post_form(url, headers, params)
reference.description: Send form fields supplied as a VARCHAR-to-VARCHAR map.

reference.name: response->>'status'
reference.description: Read the status; ->>'body' extracts the body text.

reference.name: response->'headers'->>'content-type'
reference.description: Read one response header from the JSON object.

reference.name: SET http_client_max_response_size
reference.description: Cap bodies (100 MiB); http_client_max_redirects defaults to 10.

notes.title: DuckDB’s HTTP stack
notes.body: https:// and methods other than plain GET need httpfs (autoloaded). http_timeout, http_retries, http_proxy and HTTP secrets apply. Nothing is sent while enable_external_access is false; https:// never redirects to http://.

notes.title: Inspect status before parsing
notes.body: Requests are synchronous; save responses to a table before repeated analysis. A body can be HTML, text or JSON, and non-UTF-8 bodies arrive base64-encoded with body_encoding. Check status before casting; an HTTP error is not an API result.

examples.title: Fetch once, inspect locally
examples.caption: Requires network access. The example.com response is HTML, so keep body as text.

examples.title: POST a JSON document
examples.caption: Replace the URL with your POST endpoint and add required authentication headers.
examples.reason: Requires a configured HTTP endpoint and sends data to it.

examples.title: Decode a JSON response body
examples.caption: Offline envelope fixture; returns the text value 42.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN ((('{"body":"{\"count\":42}"}'::JSON->>'body')::JSON)->>'count') = '42' THEN true ELSE error('HTTP envelope decode failed') END;
